cover letter
Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training.

Under the general direction of the Institute Director(s), the Administrative Officer serves as the primary administrative and operations professional for the Nancy Pelosi Institute for Representative Democracy, a research institute housed within the Charles and Louise Travers Department of Political Science at UC Berkeley. The position provides comprehensive administrative, operational, financial, communications, and programmatic support to advance the Institute's mission of strengthening democratic institutions through research, teaching, civic engagement, leadership development, and public programming.

Leads the planning, coordination, and execution of the Nancy Pelosi Institute's conferences, lecture series, policy forums, research symposia, donor cultivation events, executive meetings, educational programs, student engagement initiatives, and other high-profile public events.

This position works collaboratively with Institute and Department leadership, faculty, researchers, staff, students, campus partners, donors, policymakers, and external organizations, the incumbent coordinates high-profile conferences, speaker series, policy forums, workshops, visiting scholars, and public events; manages institute communications, travel, and day-to-day operations; provides project management support for strategic initiatives; maintains administrative records and reporting; and supports the Institute's digital presence and outreach efforts. The Administrative Officer ensures that Institute activities are executed efficiently, professionally, and in compliance with University and departmental policies while advancing the research, educational, and public service missions of both the Nancy Pelosi Institute for Representative Democracy and the Charles and Louise Travers Department of Political Science.

Serves as the primary administrator responsible for all logistical and operational aspects of Institute programming, independently managing multiple complex projects simultaneously by developing comprehensive project plans and timelines, coordinating stakeholders, monitoring milestones, anticipating and resolving logistical challenges, and implementing contingency plans to ensure successful execution within established deadlines and budget parameters.

Coordinates all event logistics, including venue selection and reservations, room configuration, audiovisual production, livestreaming and hybrid meeting technology, registration management, accessibility accommodations, security coordination, catering, transportation, lodging, travel arrangements, parking, speaker itineraries, protocol for distinguished guests, and the preparation of event materials.

Collaborates with faculty, campus departments, external organizations, vendors, and service providers to deliver professional, seamless events that advance the Institute's mission and provide an exceptional experience for policymakers, donors, researchers, students, and other distinguished participants.

Develops, administers, and monitors comprehensive event budgets, including forecasting expenditures, tracking actual costs, reconciling expenses, and preparing financial reports for Institute leadership.

Exercises independent judgment in allocating resources, identifying cost-saving opportunities, recommending budget adjustments, and ensuring all expenditures comply with University financial, procurement, entertainment, and travel policies while maximizing the impact of Institute programming.

Compiles, maintains, and analyzes data related to Institute events, activities, funding, research outputs, program outcomes, participation, and financial operations, preparing reports, metrics, and post-event analyses that support strategic planning, informed decision-making, continuous program improvement, and the accuracy and integrity of Institute records.

Provides comprehensive executive and administrative support to the Executive Director by independently managing a complex calendar; scheduling and prioritizing meetings, conferences, speaking engagements, donor visits, and strategic initiatives; resolving scheduling conflicts; and coordinating with internal and external stakeholders to ensure the Executive Director's time is aligned with the Institute's operational, academic, and strategic priorities.

Coordinates complex domestic and international travel for the Executive Director, affiliated faculty, researchers, visiting scholars, advisory board members, and distinguished guest speakers by developing detailed itineraries, arranging transportation and lodging, coordinating meeting schedules and event logistics, and ensuring compliance with University travel, reimbursement, and risk management policies.

Researches, drafts, edits, and proofreads correspondence, reports, presentations, briefing materials, donor communications, and other written communications on behalf of Institute leadership and affiliated faculty, ensuring accuracy, professionalism, confidentiality, and alignment with the Institute's mission and strategic objectives.

In consultation with the Executive Director, coordinates the work of undergraduate student assistants by assigning projects, establishing priorities and deadlines, providing training and guidance, monitoring progress, and ensuring the timely completion of administrative, research support, communications, and event-related assignments.
Regularly assesses competing administrative, operational, and programmatic priorities to ensure Institute activities are completed on time.
Independently reprioritizes work, adjusts schedules, and reallocates resources when event requirements, leadership priorities, or stakeholder needs change unexpectedly.

Evaluates existing workflows and develops or revises administrative procedures, tracking systems, or communication processes to improve operational efficiency, support new Institute initiatives, and ensure compliance with evolving University policies and best practices.

Collaborates closely with the Executive Director (Ed) to develop and implement strategic communications that advance the mission, priorities, and public profile of the Nancy Pelosi Institute for Representative Democracy (NPI).

Coordinates the planning, development, and continuous enhancement of the Institute's website, newsletters, marketing materials, social media, annual reports, and other public-facing communications, ensuring consistent messaging and alignment with the Institute's strategic goals.
Serves as the primary liaison with vendors, service providers, campus procurement, facilities, information technology, communications, and hospitality partners.

Researches and resolves vendor issues, negotiates service expectations, coordinates contracts and purchase orders, monitors vendor performance, processes invoices and reimbursements, and ensures timely payment in accordance with University policies and contractual obligations.
Interpersonal skills, including verbal and written communication, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising, and counseling skills.

Thorough knowledge (or comparable institutional knowledge) of University rules and regulations, processes, protocols, and procedures for budget, accounting, and fund management, and/or personnel management.

Knowledge of a variety of administrative operational activities such as event planning, basic fundraising processes, risk management planning, website design, accounting and payroll, and contracts and grants regulations and guidelines.
Solid knowledge of University-specific computer application programs or comparable systems.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
Strong skills in short-term planning, analysis, problem-solving, and customer service.
Thorough knowledge of financial analysis and reporting techniques, and/or human resources policies and procedures for staff and academic employees.
